issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, no hard-coded answer. The change only adds a new random move to the existing search loop. On 15% of iterations it picks a pair of touching circles and pushes the two apart along the line between their centres. The packing is still computed and checked by the harness.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Centres are clipped back into [0,1], and if no pair of circles is touching it falls back to choosing from all pairs. Adding the new branch shifts the odds of the existing moves: the old 50/50 split now applies only to the remaining 85% of iterations. This is a design choice, not an error.
Minor: np.triu_indices and all pairwise distances are recomputed on every bond move. That costs a little time inside the fixed 215 s loop but is harmless with 26 circles.
The loop stops on the clock, so results can vary by about 1e-6 between runs even with a seed. With only 1 run each, the result is not well resolved.

The numbers match. Both candidate and incumbent score -2.636, so the difference is 0 and z = 0. The variance can't be estimated from one run each, but a zero difference gives z = 0 in any case. 2.636 is consistent with the best known 2.635 (about 2.6358 before rounding), so it is not suspicious. Rejecting is the right call because the candidate shows no improvement.
